study type: Retrospective comparative analysis of surgical logbook data
exposure: Surgical training received by Australian general surgical trainees
Surgical procedures performed by Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) surgeons during humanitarian missions
outcome: Types and numbers of surgical procedures performed by Australian general surgical trainees
Types and numbers of surgical procedures performed by MSF surgeons
cohort: The study compared surgical logbook data from Australian general surgical trainees with data from Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) surgeons deployed during sudden-onset disasters.
finding: Australian general surgical trainees receive exposure to essential and advanced general surgery but lack exposure to specialty procedures, including obstetric and orthopedic procedures, commonly performed by MSF surgeons after sudden-onset disasters.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections were a common procedure (12.5%) performed by MSF surgeons in sudden-onset disasters, indicating a gap in exposure for Australian general surgical trainees.
cross-section timing: Australian general surgical trainee data: February 2008 to February 2017; MSF surgeon data: 6 months following each disaster (2010 Haiti earthquake, 2013 Philippines typhoon, 2015 Nepal earthquake).
